extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for inventorship, supplemental oaths/declarations, substitute statements, and applicant identity in U.S. patent applications (post- and pre‑AIA distinctions included). Covers when and how inventorship and oath/declaration issues must be corrected or substituted and who may act as applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventorship contribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each named inventor must have made a contribution, individually or jointly, to the subject matter of at least one claim of the (nonprovisional) application; for provisional applications, each named inventor must have made a contribution to the subject matter disclosed in the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple inventors may be named even if they did not work together, did not work at the same time, did not make the same type or amount of contribution, or did not contribute to every claim. See 35 U.S.C. 116 and MPEP discussion. Examiner should assume subject matter of claims was commonly owned at time inventions were made unless evidence to the contrary; inquiry into inventors/dates should be delayed until necessary for proper examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship when claims change
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are responsible for correcting inventorship in compliance with 37 CFR 1.48 when the application is amended to change the claims so that one (or more) of the named inventors is no longer an inventor of the subject matter of a claim remaining in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests under 37 CFR 1.48 filed on or after September 16, 2012 are treated by OPAP; if granted, OPAP will correct Office records and send a corrected filing receipt. Examiner should remind applicants of necessity to correct inventorship if restriction/election results in claims not belonging to all originally named inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-invention requirement and restriction practice (35 U.S.C. 121)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must be directed to only a single invention; if joint inventors' application includes more than one independent and distinct invention, restriction may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction can result in need to change inventorship if the elected invention was not the invention of all originally named inventors. A divisional application complying with 35 U.S.C. 120 may be entitled to benefit of earlier filing date. Examiner should remind applicants to correct inventorship pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48 if election cancels claims of some inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner presumptions regarding ownership and inquiry timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is filed with joint inventors, the examiner should assume that the subject matter of the various claims was commonly owned at the time the inventions covered therein were made, unless there is evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should not inquire of the applicant concerning the inventors and invention dates for various claims until necessary to properly examine the application. The Office or a court may later inquire regarding inventorship or ownership on effective filing date or invention date as applicable (37 CFR 1.110).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental inventor's oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.67) — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit an inventor's oath or declaration meeting the requirements of § 1.63, § 1.64, or § 1.162 to correct any deficiencies or inaccuracies present in an earlier-filed inventor's oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies due to failure to meet § 1.63(b) may be corrected with an application data sheet under § 1.76, except corrections of inventorship must be pursuant to § 1.48. A supplemental oath/declaration must be executed by the person whose oath/declaration is being withdrawn, replaced, or corrected. No new matter may be introduced into a nonprovisional application even if a supplemental oath/declaration is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath/declaration signature rules (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012 (pre-AIA), deficiencies or inaccuracies relating to all inventors/applicants must be corrected with a supplemental oath/declaration signed by all inventors/applicants; if related to fewer than all, signed only by those to whom the error relates; certain data errors may be corrected with an application data sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA supplemental oath must include substantially all data called for in pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63. Examples clarify when only one inventor's signature suffices (e.g., correcting citizenship of one inventor) versus when all must sign (e.g., adding omitted duty-to-disclose clause). If an inventor who executed original declaration refuses or cannot be found, the signature requirement may be suspended or waived under 37 CFR 1.183; available joint inventors must sign on behalf of nonsigning inventor, or a party with sufficient proprietary interest must sign if no joint inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter introduced by supplemental oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter may be introduced into a nonprovisional application after its filing date even if an inventor's oath or declaration is filed to correct deficiencies or inaccuracies present in the earlier-filed oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental oaths/declarations cannot be used to add substantive disclosure; they are procedural corrections only (37 CFR 1.67(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing supplemental oaths after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental oaths and declarations covering the claims in the application may be filed after allowance as a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When received they are placed in the file by the Office of Data Management, but receipt will not be acknowledged. They should not be filed or considered as amendments under 37 CFR 1.312, since they make no change in the wording of the papers on file (see MPEP § 714.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement in lieu of oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.64) — permitted circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant under § 1.43, 1.45 or 1.46 may execute a substitute statement in lieu of an oath or declaration under § 1.63 if the inventor is deceased, is under a legal incapacity, has refused to execute the oath or declaration under § 1.63, or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.64 implements 35 U.S.C. 115(d) for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012. Substitute statements are applicable only in the listed permitted circumstances; substitute statements must comply with other § 1.64 content and signature rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement content and identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement must: (1) comply with § 1.63(a), identifying the inventor(s) and stating upon information and belief the facts the inventor must state; (2) identify the person executing the statement and their relationship to the inventor and (unless supplied in an ADS) the residence and mailing address of the person signing; (3) identify the circumstances permitting execution (deceased, incapacitated, refused, or cannot be found); and (4) unless in an ADS, identify each inventor's legal name and last known mailing address and residence for each inventor not deceased or under legal incapacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international design applications certain identification requirements may be satisfied by information presented prior to international registration (37 CFR 1.1021(d)(3)). When an assignee executes a substitute statement, use assignee's residence/mailing address; if assignee is juristic entity include applicant name and signer title and show authority. A power of attorney to a practitioner does not make the practitioner an official able to sign a substitute statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement signatory qualifications and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may not execute a substitute statement unless that person has reviewed and understands the contents of the application, including the claims, and is aware of the duty to disclose to the Office all information known to the person to be material to patentability (as defined in § 1.56).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-inventor applicant is not required to state in the substitute statement that he/she has reviewed the application, but the substantive requirement remains that the signer must have reviewed and understood the application. The substitute statement must contain an acknowledgment that any willful false statement is punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 (fine or imprisonment up to 5 years). A nonsigning inventor may later join by submitting an oath or declaration under § 1.63.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign substitute statement on behalf of an inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted signers include: the inventor’s legal representative (for deceased/incapacitated inventors) under § 1.43; other joint inventors under § 1.45 (if the inventor refuses or cannot be found); an assignee or person to whom inventor is under obligation to assign, or a person showing sufficient proprietary interest under § 1.46, in appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples clarify when legal representative vs. joint inventors vs. assignee may sign. Where multiple assignees together are the applicant, all must execute the substitute statement on behalf of the non-signing inventor. Proof of the permitted circumstance is not required to be submitted to the Office, but attempts to secure inventor's signature should be documented and kept in applicant's file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant identity and who may be the applicant (37 CFR 1.42–1.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'applicant' refers to the inventor or all joint inventors, or to the person applying under §§ 1.43, 1.45, or 1.46. A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign, or a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest, may be the applicant under § 1.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant is a person other than the inventor under § 1.46, the application must contain an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying the assignee or person with proprietary interest in the applicant information section. Documentary evidence of ownership should be recorded no later than issue fee payment. If a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest files, they must submit a petition with fee, a showing of proprietary interest, and a statement that filing is appropriate to preserve parties' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration execution requirement despite non-inventor applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if whole or part interest in the invention is assigned, an oath or declaration must be executed by the actual inventor or each actual joint inventor, except as provided for in § 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a substitute statement under § 1.64 by an assignee or other non-inventor is an exception; otherwise the inventor(s) must execute the oath/declaration in accordance with § 1.63.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change or correction of applicant name or change in applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or update the name of the applicant must include an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying the correct or updated name in the applicant information section; any request to change the applicant after an original applicant has been specified must include an ADS and comply with §§ 3.71 and 3.73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change in the name of the applicant recorded pursuant to Hague Agreement Article 16(1)(ii) will be effective to change the name in a nonprovisional international design application. Follow ADS procedures in § 1.76(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office discretion to require additional information on ownership/authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require additional information where there is a question concerning ownership or interest in an application, and a showing may be required that the filing was authorized where such authorization comes into question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a real party in interest has filed under § 1.46, applicant must notify the Office of any change in real party in interest no later than payment of the issue fee; absence of notice will be treated as indication no change occurred. Office may publish notice of filing by a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the Official Gazette.
